paragraphs: Chapter 815
204th Episode. Declaration of War (2)
Ziffel, Drakka.
"Our Imperial City is under attack from the Red Army. Our provocation will lose its power."
Verradin commented while perusing the report. Ziffel's informants hadn't directly witnessed the battle, but they confirmed that the city had become ruins.

Next to the report were newsletters. The newsletters from the Rutherford Federation all incited content that Jin and the Barmel Alliance were waking up the Red Army and threatening the human world. Meanwhile, the newsletters from Hufester detailed the victory of the city.

The contrast was inevitable. Even comparing only the damage, Ziffel lost a 2nd-class magic tower, while the Barmel Alliance lost the city but rescued most of the reserve knights and dragons and defeated Drekk and his fleet.
"Hufester has not been able to produce a proper rebuttal article about the fact that the Red Army woke up due to Jin Lun Candle. I think we should focus on this point."

"Proceed as you say, Brother Ronil. Anyway, the most important thing to reduce the effort when we revise history ourselves in the future is that part. However, due to this incident, the public will once again feel that we are more incompetent than the Barmel Alliance. It hurts more because it's true."

"......The problem is the technology. The Barmel Alliance seems to have secured a long-distance communication method in addition to teleportation. It's what the spies we planted in the Empire confirmed."
At Satrin's words, Verradin nodded.

"If the previous head of the house had taken care of Valeria Hister in time and kept Tinggen Bauer well, the technology gap would not have been this big. The only possibility for us to make a leap in technology like the Barmel Alliance is to steal it from the Red Army. Because the chaos control technology we invested in until just before the beast temple is almost useless now."
The problem was that they didn't know the base of the Red Army at all.

"......It's frustrating. The Red Army completely holds the right to attack first, so we basically have no choice but to wait for their invasion if we want to analyze their technology. All we can do is examine the remains after the battle, Lord. Of course, it would be a bit better if we could capture the Red Army alive in any way."

"Even that, we'll inevitably be later than the Barmel Alliance. Jin must have already obtained quite a lot of Red Army's things or debris through the battles with the 3rd Region of Kinzel and the dragon city. Valeria Hister and Tinggen Bauer are likely to be analyzing diligently. And with this defeat, they've probably become more afraid of Jin. Do you all understand what that means?"
Verradin looked around the executives with his eyes narrowed.

"It means that there's a very high probability that the Red Army will only target us and Kinzel in the future. However, since Kinzel has confirmed that Jin comes out unexpectedly when they invade, they must have judged that it's safer to hit us among the two."
The atmosphere in the meeting room grew heavy.
"Lord, have you heard anything from the Shaman?"

"No, Captain of Ghosts. She said she's deep in prayer and feels she'll have some revelation soon. Finding out the whereabouts of the previous Lord and the Red Army's base, those two things are up to the Shaman."
Naturally, Ziffel was still tracking Kelliac Ziffel. This was because they could accelerate the completion of the magic stone by completely ending Kelliac and Shinu.
"If the Shaman can do that...... What we need is time. Until the Shaman gets the result."
The moment Octavia said that, a commotion came from the corridor.
"What's the commotion!"
A sitting executive yelled and a doorkeeper mage entered.
"Lord! The Red Army's ships are now circling the Federation and scattering these papers......!"
"What? Are you saying their ships are flying over Federation airspace!?"
"Give it here."
The paper that the gatekeeper handed to Verradin in a hurry contained the following content.
(To the humans of the Rutherford Magic Federation.
From this moment, we, the Red Army, declare war on the Rutherford Magic Federation on the surface.
The Federation can never handle us.
However, when the war ends with our victory, there will be more than just blood, death, and the scars of war left in the Federation.
Before officially starting the war, we make two promises to ordinary humans who are not members of the 'Federal Army'.

First, we will wage war while excluding civilian casualties. We are conquerors, not slaughterers. Soldiers, too, will be treated fairly as civilians as soon as they surrender. Only soldiers will die from our swords and bombardment. Absolutely, there will be no cases of civilians being slaughtered.

Secondly, after the war, we will dramatically advance the civilization of the Rutherford Magic Federation. The entire Federation will be redesigned with the superior technology and resources of the Red Army, and ordinary people will be able to equally enjoy all the benefits.
Our next goal is one of Ziffel's 1st-class magic towers. Within a week, you will lose one of the 1st-class magic towers.
Prepare as much as you can.
The Red Army will make this world whole again. -Bakarun Jung, King of the Red Army Battles.)
The executives who examined the paper blinked their eyes for a moment, forgetting to speak.
Looking at the message alone, it seemed the Red Army was already confident of their complete victory.
"They're kind enough to even tell us their next target."
Verradin spoke in a calm voice, but the executives barely suppressed their anger. For the past thousand years, Ziffel had never received such provocation.
"What happened to the Red Army's ships that scattered the papers?"

"I only saw those that appeared in Phelan. The Federation fleet immediately tried to shoot them down, but they managed to escape without any significant damage. The speed difference was so significant that our large ships were completely unable to pursue, and the small high-speed ships couldn't break through their defenses to continue the chase."
"It seems there was nothing we could do given the difference in ship technology. And there are currently no Superhumans on standby in Phelan."
"Yes, my lord."
"Understood."
A moment of silence followed as the magician who brought the paper left. Verradin looked at the executives in contemplation for a moment.
"Immediately switch all the first-class magic towers in the Federation to full combat readiness and recall the major ships that are currently dispatched."
"What should we do about the civilians near the magic towers?"
"Quarantine them. So they can't evacuate. Let's see if they really do exclude civilian casualties in their warfare."
In saying this, Verradin seemed to be planning to use civilians like hostages. He seemed to understand why the Red Army emphasized in their declaration of war that they wouldn't harm civilians.

"The results so far have told us. We hardly have any areas where we are superior to the Red Army in the war. We are infinitely lacking in fleet performance, communication means, and mobility. So we need to buy time to use what we've prepared so far. Use the civilians as a shield."
"Do you think we, Ziffel, won't even be able to buy that time if they unhesitatingly slaughter civilians contrary to their declaration of war, my lord?"
"That will depend on how powerful the Red Army really is, Captain of Ghosts. However, even if they do massacre the civilians, it won't be so bad for us."
"Why is that?"
"Because if they do such a thing, Jin won't be able to just stand by and watch our war with the Red Army."
Verradin answered with a cold smile.
[The declaration of war reveals how much the Red Army fears you.]
Ameris said.
Ticano was also conducting a meeting as soon as he acquired the Red Army's declaration of war.
[They're sure that if they massacre civilians, even if they're Federation members, you won't stand idly by. That's why they emphasized this content, to avoid your involvement in this war.]

The Red Army has been collecting information from the ground since Shimat and his group were unsealed. Naturally, they also looked at the public records of the Fenster Shrine, and they learned from the Bement royal family how not to provoke Jin.
That is the absolute principle of never touching civilians.

In reality, if civilians were massacred by the Red Army, Jin wouldn't hesitate to support them immediately. It's the appropriate duty as a regressor, as a human who now governs one axis of this world.
In other words, even if it's a full-scale war between the current largest underground force and the oldest loser on the surface.
Civilians could be guaranteed an unbelievable level of safety during the war. All thanks to the influence of one man, Jin Runkendel.
Of course, because it is war.

Civilians of the Lutero Magic Federation would inevitably suffer in some way. They could lose family members in the military and lose their livelihoods and homes. But the important thing is that mass slaughter is completely prohibited.

Therefore, as long as the Red Army adheres to what they have declared themselves, the situation wouldn't be bad for the Barmel Union. Purely, because the 'enemies' are fighting each other, shedding blood.

"At the last meeting, I said that what we needed most was time. Time to produce fleets and distribute communication devices across the region, time to complete the mass-produced Ielo and the magic knight squad, time to figure out what means the enemies possess, time until Murakan returns, time to finish a way for my brothers to come out. And now, it seems that an opportunity to buy that time has come."
As Jin spoke, his colleagues looked at him.

"If the Red Army and Ziffel maintain the declaration of war, the war between the two forces can only be a stalemate. The Red Army can't indiscriminately shell due to civilians, and Ziffel doesn't know their base, so they have no initiative. The key moment will be when one side finds a clue."
From the Red Army's position, a situation would be created where they no longer have to worry about Jin.
From Ziffel's position, a situation would be created where they could find their base and win by sticking to it with all their might.
Those two elements were the core of this war. Until one of the two is established, the Barmel Union can prepare for the war that will inevitably expand in the future.

"We must immediately issue a statement. As long as they don't massacre civilians, we will never participate in the war. And we should also add that we won't skimp on material support for the civilians isolated in the Federation. We'll need to see the first battle firsthand, so start preparing a team to infiltrate each first-class magic tower."
